warnings: (Shader/Lookdev – biggest win) Add/drive a temperature-based color map (Blackbody or ColorRamp) so only the hottest regions go near-white/yellow, with cooler regions going orange/red and outer smoke going dark. If you don’t have a temperature attribute yet, consider authoring one (or deriving from density/height) so color isn’t uniform.
Increase volumetric forward scattering to get a brighter, more “fiery” glow in the core while keeping edges smoky: Line 280 pv.inputs['Anisotropy'] from 0.15 → 0.4–0.7 (test increments).

Push the volume toward a hotter core color (even if it’s only a partial fix without true emission control): Line 274 pv.inputs['Color'] from (0.12,0.12,0.13,1) → try something warmer/brighter like (0.8,0.55,0.25,1) or (1.0,0.8,0.5,1), then re-balance density/absorption to avoid a flat glow.

Add more internal contrast (smoky shadowing) by increasing absorption relative to scatter: Line 281 pv.inputs['Absorption Color'] from (0.05,0.05,0.055,1) → try (0.12,0.12,0.13,1) for stronger extinction, then compensate with emission/core brightness (preferably via temperature) so it doesn’t just go dark.

Reduce the “single-scale blob” look by changing procedural detail scales:
- Line 247 noise.inputs['Scale'] 25.0 → try 40–80 for finer breakup (or add a second noise at lower scale if available).
- Line 248 noise.inputs['Detail'] 4.0 → try 6–10 to introduce smaller eddies.
- Line 113 noise.inputs['Roughness'] 0.55 → try 0.7–0.85 to increase high-frequency contribution.

Rebalance the noise mixing so you get both large licks and small turbulence: Line 174 mix.inputs['Factor'] 0.6 → test 0.35–0.5 (more influence from the secondary pattern if it adds breakup) or 0.7–0.8 (if the secondary pattern is currently harming structure).

Tune wave deformation so it creates flame tongues rather than broad warping:
- Line 164 wave.inputs['Scale'] 14.0 → test 20–35 for more frequent tongues.
- Line 165 wave.inputs['Distortion'] 6.0 → test 2–4 if distortion is smearing forms; or 7–10 if it’s currently too smooth (pick the direction that creates sharper breakup).

If the bump is contributing to “mushy” shading rather than detail, either strengthen it for clearer surface breakup or disable it: Line 205 bump.inputs['Strength'] 0.15 → test 0.25–0.4 (more crisp) or 0.05 (less blobby shading).
Mitigate banding/posterization: render to 16/32-bit (EXR) and keep the fire in HDR; add bloom/glare only to the hottest core (not the entire volume).

Background/scene integration: if the environment light is flattening contrast, reduce it: Line 66 bg.inputs['Strength'] 0.2 → test 0.05–0.12 so the flame reads hotter against a darker scene (then rely on flame lighting for local illumination).
